title: Reverse diffusion process
reading: The slide introduces the reverse (denoising) direction of diffusion models: after noise has been progressively added in the forward process, a neural network known as a denoiser is trained to undo it step by step. The accompanying note emphasises that each individual denoising step can be framed as a supervised learning problem, since the noisy input and the corresponding clean (or less noisy) target are both known during training.

concepts.name: Reverse diffusion process
concepts.why_it_matters: It is the generative half of a diffusion model, turning noise into data.

concepts.name: Denoiser network
concepts.why_it_matters: The learned component that performs each reverse step.

concepts.name: Supervised learning framing of denoising
concepts.why_it_matters: Explains why diffusion training is stable and simple: paired noisy/clean data is generated for free.

concepts.name: Forward diffusion (noising) process
concepts.why_it_matters: The reverse process is defined relative to it.

verbatim_spans: Diffusion models then train a neural network (denoiser) to reverse this process
